newsitem.title: CANADA: Amber Energy plans Alberta oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Amber Energy plans Alberta oil pipeline.

text.p: Amber Energy Inc said on Wednesday it planned to build a 100,000 barrels a day pipeline to transport heavy oil from the Pelican Lake field in northeastern Alberta

Amber, whose stock has soared on expected production growth from the sought-after play, said it would build the 16-inch-diameter oil pipeline, a condensate supply line and terminal facilies at Mitsue and Wabasca, Alberta at a cost of C$47 million.
The line would be partially operational by April and fully operational late next year, it said.
The project is the latest of several announced over the past few months to transport fast-growing volumes of heavy oil from northeastern Alberta.

Other pipelines have been proposed by Alberta Energy Co Ltd and Husky Oil Ltd as well as Suncor Energy Inc and IPL Energy Inc. Imperial Oil Ltd said two weeks ago it was also considering a pipeline from its Cold Lake, Alberta bitumen operation.
Amber said it would file regulatory applications shortly and solicit nominations for capacity from other producers in the area.

Besides Amber, companies with operations at Pelican Lake include Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd and CS Resources, now a subsidiary of PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd. Alberta Energy and Canadian Natural Resources Ltd recently shelled out far higher than average money to acquire acreage there.

Pelican Lake, which has an estimated three billion barrels of heavy oil in place, including 400 million recoverable barrels barrels, has been described as the largest oilfield found in Alberta since 1964.

Amber earlier reported six-month earnings of C$7.8 million or 15 cents a share on revenues of C$50.7 million, up from C$6.4 million or 13 cents a share on revenues of C$34.4 million in the same period last year.
Cash flow in the first half totalled C$28.3 million or 53 cetns a share, up from C$21.1 million or 43 cents a share in 1996. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
